name: Margaret Ellison
presenting_complaint: Fever, productive cough and right-sided pleuritic chest pain for 3 days, now breathless and drowsy

medical_history.social: Ex-smoker, 40 pack-year history, quit 5 years ago. Lives alone, independent. Occasional alcohol.

validation_criteria.presenting_scenario: A 72-year-old woman presents to ED with 3 days of fever, productive cough with rusty sputum and right-sided pleuritic chest pain, now increasingly breathless and mildly confused. She has a background of mild COPD and is an ex-smoker with a 40 pack-year history. Obs: BP 104/62, HR 112, RR 30, SpO2 89% on room air, temp 38.9C, GCS 14. She looks unwell and is working hard to breathe.
validation_criteria.task: Document your assessment and initial management as the admitting RMO.

subjective: History of presenting complaint: 3 days fever, productive cough with rusty/purulent sputum, right-sided pleuritic chest pain, progressive dyspnoea and new confusion
Screen for severity/sepsis features: new confusion, reduced urine output, rigors, drowsiness — quantify with a named severity score
Risk factors and comorbidities: mild COPD, 40 pack-year ex-smoker, age >65, lives alone (affects site-of-care decision)
Key negatives: no recent travel or aspiration event, no haemoptysis, no calf pain/PE risk, no immunosuppression
Vaccination status (pneumococcal, influenza) and current medications and allergies documented
objective: Calculate and document a severity score by name — CORB (Confusion, O2 sat <=90%, RR >=30, BP <90 systolic/<=60 diastolic) and/or SMART-COP; this case scores CORB 3 (confusion + SpO2 89% + RR 30). Note BP 104/62 does NOT meet the CORB BP criterion (SBP 104 >90, DBP 62 >60)
Respiratory exam: right basal crackles, bronchial breathing, dullness to percussion, reduced air entry, use of accessory muscles
Full obs including conscious state (GCS 14 with new confusion), capillary refill and perfusion — assess for septic shock
12-lead ECG and bedside VBG (documents hypoxia/lactate and CO2 retention risk in COPD)
Portable chest X-ray to confirm consolidation and exclude effusion/pneumothorax
assessment: Severe community-acquired pneumonia with sepsis (high CORB/SMART-COP score) — requires hospital admission, likely HDU/ICU review
Document CORB/SMART-COP score to justify severity classification and site of care — CORB 3 driven by confusion, SpO2 <=90 and RR >=30 (BP 104/62 does not meet the CORB BP criterion)
Differentials considered: pulmonary embolism, infective COPD exacerbation, aspiration pneumonia, and an underlying lung malignancy behind the pneumonia in an older ex-smoker
plan: Score severity FIRST by name (CORB and/or SMART-COP) — the score decides site of care and antibiotic choice
Take blood cultures BEFORE antibiotics, plus sputum culture and pneumococcal/Legionella urinary antigens (severe CAP)

Empirical antibiotics per eTG for SEVERE CAP without hurried delay: ceftriaxone 2 g IV daily PLUS azithromycin 500 mg IV daily (add cover for Pseudomonas/Burkholderia if tropical/structural lung disease)
Controlled oxygen titrated to SpO2 88-92% target given COPD (avoid over-oxygenation and CO2 narcosis)
Bloods: FBC, UEC, LFT, CRP, blood cultures, VBG with lactate; IV fluid resuscitation for sepsis and analgesia for pleuritic pain
Investigations and monitoring: CXR, continuous obs, urine output, VTE prophylaxis, early mobilisation and physiotherapy
Referral/disposition: admit under medical team, escalate to ICU/HDU given severity, senior review

Arrange routine follow-up chest X-ray at 6 weeks to exclude an underlying malignancy in this older ex-smoker (>50), review antibiotics at 48 h, step down to oral once afebrile and improving, offer smoking-related and vaccination advice

critical_errors: Under-triaging a severe septic CAP — managing the patient at home or on a general ward and failing to escalate to HDU/ICU review despite high-severity features (confusion, SpO2 <=90, RR >=30, sepsis)

Ignoring hypoxia or failing to give any controlled oxygen to a hypoxic, septic patient (SpO2 89%); briefly exceeding 92% to correct dangerous hypoxia while awaiting an ABG is acceptable in this mild-COPD, non-CO2-retainer patient and is NOT an auto-fail
must_not_miss: Sepsis/septic shock recognised and treated (fluids, blood cultures, antibiotics within 1 hour)
Severe CAP classified with a named score (CORB/SMART-COP) determining ICU/HDU escalation
Empirical antibiotics per eTG appropriate to severity (ceftriaxone 2 g IV + azithromycin for severe CAP)
